name: richmond-flood-demo
label: SIMULATION: seeded scenario, not live data
gauge_label: scenario value, not a live USGS reading

events.label: 911 call from a bus in Shockoe Bottom
events.explain: A 911 call from a bus in Shockoe Bottom. The Listener shows the transcript (left), Muse Spark reads it into a new incident, the three agents vote and it becomes #1 in the queue. The recommendation now sends a swift water team and an ambulance there.

events.label: Citizen photo of Dock St
events.explain: A citizen photo of Dock St. The blue overlay on the map is the flood-water mask; the Vision badge reads it as impassable, so Dock St closes (black). The agents re-vote and the route changes to cross the 14th St (Mayo) Bridge instead.

events.label: River gauge update
events.explain: The river gauge rises to 11.8 ft, near the 12 ft sample trigger. Logistics re-votes the low-lying incidents and the plan is recomputed.

events.label: 911 call: man trapped in his car at Hull St
events.explain: A new 911 call: a man trapped in his car in the Hull St underpass. The agents score it as critical, but every rescue team is already on a mission, so the recommendation shows it as waiting, with the reason. Watch what happens when a team frees up.

events.label: Swift Water Team 1: Riverside residents safe
events.text: All five residents at Riverside Apartments are out and safe.
events.explain: Swift Water Team 1 reports the Riverside residents are safe, so that incident closes and its boat and ambulance are free again. The swarm re-plans: the most urgent waiting request now gets them.

intro: Five incidents are already open. Each card shows three agent votes (Triage, Vision, Logistics) and their consensus; the queue is ranked by it. The right panel is the swarm's current recommendation. Watch the next event arrive.
outro: Your turn. Read the recommendation on the right (what, why, confidence, tradeoff) and press Approve & Dispatch. The English and Spanish public alert appears below it. The demo then keeps going: new reports keep arriving.
approved: Approved: units are dispatched (they move on the map) and the alert is out. Operations continue: more reports are on the way.
outro_2: Your turn again. A freed team can now reach the waiting call. Review the new recommendation and press Approve & Dispatch.
final: That is the full loop: detect, prioritize, decide, dispatch, communicate, and again when new information arrives. Press RESTART DEMO to run it again.
